text: Continuous integration is a software development practice where developers frequently merge their code changes into a shared main repository. Each time new code is added, an automated build process is triggered. This build compiles the code and then runs a series of tests to check for errors. The main goal is to catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. These steps are organized into what is called a CI pipeline. By using CI pipelines, teams can quickly identify and fix bugs, ensuring the software stays stable and reliable as it grows. This saves time and reduces the risk of major failures later on.
